label: Metrically finite populated pasts from spaced Grim Reaper pieces and patchwork
meaning: Non-transcription conditional support option for the metric denial of horn H2: no populated past in an accessible history is metrically infinite. Time is linearly ordered (a type-class assumption of the theorem, not a premise statement) and measured by a supplied real clock strictly increasing along it. Suppose a contingent concrete thing is present at t in an accessible history and the clock readings of the moments at or before t are unbounded below; choice gives a strictly descending sequence from t whose slots each last more than one clock unit. The spaced local premise makes every two adjacent Reaper pieces along it co-possible; spaced patchwork gives one accessible world realizing all of them; the verified GrimReaperPatchwork.arrangementImpossible, which composes IndexedSignalReaper.impossible, refutes that world. Each premise holds without the other in a beginningless integer history (control 1). The premises are silent about every metrically finite past, so they are satisfiable, for every register frame, by a populated past that is open below and finite (positive real times, control 2) and by continuous time with a first moment (non-negative real times, control 3): neither the FLRW objection nor the Benardete parity objection to the order-theoretic GrimReaperPatchwork premises has a target here. The conclusion does NOT give a past with a beginning: control 2 satisfies both premises and the conclusion with no begun populated moment, and there, with the earlier-grounded possibility premise, begun coming-to-be (A3 prime w) is not possible. Both premises are OPEN. Nothing is attributed to Koons or Pruss. No premise is established.
